punchline: After studying 35,000 sales calls, Neil Rackham found that the push to close, which works on small purchases, tends to backfire on big ones.
thirty_sec: Neil Rackham's team studied 35,000 sales calls over about twelve years and found that habits from small sales, like pressing to close, annoy buyers in large ones. So he measured success differently. A call that ends with a step the buyer agrees to, an Advance, counts. A call that ends with nothing agreed, a Continuation, is a failure even if everyone was friendly.
key_contrast: a yes versus a next step
